tools.name: list_flags
tools.description: All flags with their state in each environment.

tools.name: get_flag
tools.description: One flag: variations and full targeting in every environment, with versions for safe updates.

tools.name: list_environments
tools.description: Environments, whether they require approval, and their published config versions. Keys are not returned.

tools.name: create_flag
tools.description: Creates a flag, off in every environment. Boolean flags have variations [false, true].

tools.name: toggle_flag
tools.description: Turns a flag on or off in one environment. In environments that need approval this returns an approvalUrl for a person.

tools.name: update_targeting
tools.description: Replaces a flag's targeting in one environment. Read it with get_flag first and pass its version as baseVersion so you never overwrite someone else's change. Rules are checked top to bottom; the first match wins.

tools.name: set_rollout
tools.description: Sets the percentage split for the default rule, or for one rule by id. percentages has one number per variation and must add up to 100 (e.g. [80, 20] gives 20% true for a boolean flag). Raising a percentage only adds users.

tools.name: get_history
tools.description: Audit log for the project or one flag: who changed what, when and why.

tools.name: get_change_request
tools.description: Status of a change waiting for approval: pending, applied, rejected or failed.

tools.name: suggest_watch_plan
tools.description: Drafts a Release Watch plan for a flag change: which signals to monitor (error rate, latency, conversions, new Sentry issues, the rollout split), the limits, and for how long. Describe the change with percentages (default rule split, like set_rollout), enabled (on/off) or a full targeting. Returns a

tools.name: get_watch
tools.description: A watch: its status (draft, active, passed, paused, stopped), each signal's state, the timeline and the verdict.

tools.name: list_watches
tools.description: Watches in the project, newest first, optionally for one flag and by status (comma separated: draft, active, passed, paused, stopped, expired).

tools.name: stop_watch
tools.description: Stops watching. Doesn't change the flag.

tools.name: monitoring_coverage
tools.description: The project's monitoring coverage: live Production flags nobody watches (ranked by risk), kill switches never tested, flags no SDK evaluates, and services missing error or latency metrics. Business plan.

tools.name: connect_monitoring
tools.description: Starts connecting Prometheus/Grafana, Datadog, Sentry, New Relic or a Slack channel for alerts. Returns a one-time link: give it to the user, who enters the credentials there. Never ask the user for credentials in chat. Admins only.

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: Vendors Railflag can import flags from, what it reads from each, and which are coming later.

tools.name: connect_source
tools.description: Starts a read-only connection to the user's account at another flag vendor (see list_sources). Returns a link the user opens to enter their credentials there. Never ask the user to paste credentials into the chat. After they finish, call get_connection.

tools.name: get_connection
tools.description: Whether the user finished connecting, which source environments are visible, and whether decisions can be compared.

tools.name: scan_source
tools.description: Reads all flags and their targeting from the connected vendor (read only). Runs in the background: poll get_run with the returned runId.

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: Status and result of a scan, compare or apply run.

tools.name: plan_migration
tools.description: Builds a dry-run plan from the latest scan. envMap maps source environment ids (from get_connection or the scan) to Railflag environment keys, e.g. {"production": "staging"} to try production data in staging first. Nothing is written.

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: A plan's summary, issues and items. full=true includes each item's targeting.

tools.name: explain_item
tools.description: The source vendor's definition of one flag next to what it becomes in Railflag, and its issues.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description: Records decisions on issues. Each issue lists its allowed actions: skip_flag, drop_rule, keep, rename (value = new key), overwrite. Info issues need no decision. Ask the user when the choice is not obviously safe.

tools.name: compare_decisions
tools.description: Asks the source vendor what sample users get (AB Tasty: Decision API, needs a Decision API key on the connection; Unleash: its server-side playground) without recording anything, and compares with the plan. Runs in the background: poll get_run.

tools.name: apply_plan
tools.description: Writes the plan into one Railflag environment. Running it again changes nothing. Environments that need approval return an approvalUrl for a person. Never writes to the source vendor.

tools.name: rollback_run
tools.description: Undoes one apply run: restores previous targeting and archives flags it created.

tools.name: disconnect_source
tools.description: Deletes the stored credentials for a source connection.

tools.name: get_code_guide
tools.description: How to rewrite the source vendor's SDK calls to OpenFeature with Railflag: setup, regex patterns, before/after examples, notes. Apply it in the user's repo yourself and show them the diff.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "update_targeting" appears informational but accepts parameters (environment) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: key, environment, targeting, baseVersion, reason, watchPlanId

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "connect_monitoring" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
